## VIC options and activation: `implicit-scheme` 1 or 9, one block in $x_1$ (`ImplicitOptions`) {#sec-ch07-vic-options}

### Summary

The vertically implicit correction (VIC) treats the $x_1$ flux divergence of each column implicitly, so
vertical sound waves do not limit the step (@sec-ch07-cfl). It is one linear block-tridiagonal solve per column
(@sec-ch07-vic-assembly), weighted into each stage (@sec-ch07-vic-stage).
The scheme value is a bit field. Bit 0 makes $x_1$ implicit and bit 3 selects the full system; bits 1 and 2 only
change the time-step bound of @sec-ch07-cfl. Only the values 0, 1 and 9 build. Any other value stops the run when
the solver object is constructed. A VIC run also needs the whole $x_1$ column on one rank and a constant
gravity.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Decides whether a run has a vertically implicit correction (VIC) and its system size; @eq-ch07-vic-size.

**Data.** Reads `integration/implicit-scheme` and the two bound keys once per block; writes the type and $N$.

**Placement.** At setup; the one-block and gravity conditions at the first correction.

**Activation.** `integration/implicit-scheme`: 0 or absent (explicit), 1 (`vic-partial`), 9 (`vic-full`).

**Guarantee / limits.** Any other value is refused; $x_1$ only, one block in $x_1$, constant gravity.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch07-vic-options-tests; `test_implicit_options_type_python`, `test_hydro_options.release`, `vic_options_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C4]`.
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm{vic}}$ [-] is the integer value of `implicit-scheme` ($s$ is the RK[^rg-1c18af462152] stage) and $N$ [-] the
block size of the column system; `nb1`[^rg-1859c6a3e122] [count] is the number of blocks in $x_1$. No physical quantity enters, so
there are no units or mass basis.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive. The block size of the column system is

$$
N = 3 + 2\,\big(\lfloor n_{\mathrm{vic}}/8 \rfloor \bmod 2\big) ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-size}

and the steps that fix what a value means are:

1. *Bit 3.* $\lfloor n_{\mathrm{vic}}/8\rfloor \bmod 2$ is bit 3, so 1 gives $N=3$ and 9 gives $N=5$.
2. *The variables.* `vic-partial` solves for $(\rho, \rho v_1, E)$ and `vic-full` for
   $(\rho, \rho v_1, \rho v_2, \rho v_3, E)$, with $v_1$ the $x_1$ velocity (`[C1]`). Here $\rho$ is the total density: the
   species ride on it and are redistributed afterwards (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute). `vic-partial` does not hold
   $\rho v_2$, $\rho v_3$ fixed: it ties their increments to each cell's mass increment in the assembly
   (@eq-ch07-vic-fold) and moves them with the face transfers afterwards (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute).
3. *Which values build.* `type` names 0, 1 and 9 and refuses every other value, so a value with bit 1 or 2 set never
   builds, although the time-step bound reads those bits (`[C1]`).
4. *No round-off.* The value is an integer and $N$ a bit test, so nothing is rounded.

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-size is `size` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::size >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-options for the bits.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-options
#| fig-cap: "The value of integration/implicit-scheme as four bits. Bit 0 makes $x_1$ implicit; bit 3 selects the full $5\\times5$ system. The values that build are 0 (explicit: no solver object), 1 (vic-partial) and 9 (vic-full); any other value stops with Unsupported implicit scheme (vermillion). Bits 1 and 2 only change the time-step bound."
#| fig-alt: "Three rows of four bit boxes for the values 0, 1 and 9, with the set bits filled green, and a red note that other values are refused."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.figures.fig_vic_options import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The options come from the `integration` block, which pyharp's integrator also reads, so its keys are checked
against both readers ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}). A value of 0 returns no options at all from `from_yaml`, so 0 is
a true explicit spelling that also runs with several blocks in $x_1$ ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}).
The two bound keys without a scheme are an error, not ignored (`[C3]`). `implicit-advection-cfl` must be finite and
positive, and `shear-cfl` finite and non-negative (`[C2]`).

`HydroImpl` creates the solver object, `picorr`, only when the options exist ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). Its `reset`
calls `type`, which is what refuses an unsupported value ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::reset >}}). The
first correction then checks with `is_physical_boundary` that both $x_1$ faces of the block are physical
boundaries, since the column solve has no cross-rank coupling ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}). It also requires a constant gravity, through
`grav` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}) (`[C4]`).

: Code map of the VIC options. {#tbl-ch07-vic-options-code}

**How to use it.** The scheme is an integer in the `integration` block, not a name
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}):

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `forcing`[^rg-35bd573cb171], `const-gravity`[^rg-fdb90fff9fd8], `grav1`[^rg-6fce2ccff9c4].
```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -9.8}   # the solve needs a constant gravity
integration:
  type: rk3
  implicit-scheme: 1             # 0 or absent: explicit; 1: vic-partial (N = 3); 9: vic-full (N = 5)
```

What is refused, and why:

- A non-integer value such as `{type: vic}` is a YAML conversion error ("bad conversion"), because the reader takes
  `node.as<int>()`.
- Any value other than 0, 1 or 9 stops at construction with "Unsupported implicit scheme", because no other value
  has a solver ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::type >}}).
- At the first correction, a block that is not the whole $x_1$ column stops with "[Hydro] implicit scheme requires
  nb1 = 1 (no x1 decomposition): the vertical solve has no cross-rank coupling."
  ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}).
- At the first correction, a run without constant gravity stops with "[ImplicitHydro] forcing does not have
  const-gravity", because the operator carries the gravity Jacobian of @sec-ch06
  ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).

On a build of the pin, values 1 and 9 build, 3 gives "Unsupported implicit scheme", `{type: vic}` gives "bad
conversion", and a card without gravity still builds, so that refusal comes only at the first
correction.[^ch07-vic-options-card] The last two refusals were read from the code, not run. @eq-ch07-vic-size is

```cpp
  int size() const {
    if ((scheme() >> 3) & 1) {  // full
      return 5;
    } else {
      return 3;
    }
  }
```

where `(scheme() >> 3) & 1` is $\lfloor n_{\mathrm{vic}}/8\rfloor \bmod 2$ of step 1.

[^ch07-vic-options-card]: `MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml` and `MeshBlock` on the card with geometry, an ideal-moist
    equation of state and reflecting $x_1$ walls added; snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 Release build,
    CPU, Python 3.12.10.

and 10; `[C2]` gives the defaults 1 and 0 and refuses 4 of 4 bad values; `[C3]` refuses the bound keys without a
scheme; `[C4]` builds `nb1` = 1, refuses `nb1` = 2, and runs scheme 0 at `nb1` = 2. The option logic has no device
path.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The VIC is $x_1$ only. A run cut into several blocks in $x_1$ cannot use it.
:::

1. **Bits that do not build.** Bits 1 and 2 are read by the time-step bound, but no value that sets them builds,
   so a $x_2$ or $x_3$ implicit direction cannot be reached.
2. **Late checks.** The one-block and gravity conditions are checked at the first correction, not when the options
   are read, so a deck that breaks them builds and stops on its first step.

[^rg-1859c6a3e122]: nb1 — number of blocks along the first coordinate direction

[^rg-35bd573cb171]: forcing — forcing options block: a map with one sub-block per forcing component

[^rg-fdb90fff9fd8]: const-gravity — constant-gravity forcing component

[^rg-6fce2ccff9c4]: grav1 — gravity component along the first coordinate
